text:
Roger McQueen is the 6-foot-5 rookie Anaheim drafted 10th in 2025, after a season at Providence College, and he's getting a careful introduction: 11 and a half minutes a night, a little power-play time, two goals and three points in 15 games. Ryan Wilson of Hockey Hot Stove wrote that the Ducks "likely have something" with him, noting how he handles the puck. "6'5" with hands is a good start."

His numbers are about what you'd expect from a 20-year-old on the fourth line. His chance rate (0.91 individual expected goals per 60) is good for that role, and his shooting is normal. The Ducks' results with him on are even, though they've scored a couple fewer goals than their chances.

For context, forwards picked 8th to 12th since 2005 put up a median 0.37 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.20. That gap is mostly ice time. His minutes have dipped lately, about two a night below his early average. What we'd watch is whether the coaches start giving the size and hands more of the game.
